hem-iron-deficiency-anemia.title: Iron deficiency anemia
hem-iron-deficiency-anemia.blurb: Three months of fatigue and exertional breathlessness, confirmed with iron studies with ferritin measurement.
hem-iron-deficiency-anemia.summary: Iron deficiency anemia presents with three months of fatigue and exertional breathlessness, typically with conjunctival pallor with spoon-shaped nails and a craving for ice. Iron studies with ferritin measurement confirms it, and oral iron replacement with a search for the source of loss is the initial management.

sections.heading: Overview
paras: The presentation that names iron deficiency anemia is three months of fatigue and exertional breathlessness; the process behind it is depleted iron stores limiting hemoglobin synthesis. This entry is arranged in the order the problem tends to be encountered: what drives it, how it appears, how it is confirmed, and what is done first.

How often the problem is seen depends on where the counting is done, and case definitions have shifted enough over time that historical series need reading with care. The teaching point most often attached to this topic is that in an older adult, the anemia is the symptom — the digestive tract is the question.

sections.heading: Mechanism
paras: At the centre of the problem is depleted iron stores limiting hemoglobin synthesis. Its consequences account for both the symptoms the patient reports and the signs found on examination.

Compensatory responses mask the process early and fail late, which is why the interval between the first abnormality and the first symptom can be long. Understanding this is what makes oral iron replacement with a search for the source of loss the rational first response rather than an arbitrary one.

sections.heading: Clinical presentation
paras: Patients most often describe three months of fatigue and exertional breathlessness, and it is the tempo of that history — how quickly it arrived and whether it is progressing — that carries the diagnostic weight.

Partial or atypical presentations are common enough that the absence of one expected feature should not close the question. A history of three months of fatigue and exertional breathlessness in the right context is enough to bring the diagnosis to the front of the differential.

sections.heading: Examination
paras: The sign to look for is conjunctival pallor with spoon-shaped nails and a craving for ice; it is more specific than the rest of the examination and is worth eliciting carefully.
Findings are easier to elicit once the process is established, so an unrevealing first examination deserves repeating.

sections.heading: Diagnosis
paras: Iron studies with ferritin measurement is the initial study, chosen because it confirms the diagnosis and separates it from the alternatives that present the same way.

A negative result is only as useful as the probability it was applied to, which is the argument for estimating that probability first. The alternative most often confused with it is chronic myeloid leukemia, which is compared below.

hem-vitamin-b12-deficiency.title: Vitamin B12 deficiency
hem-vitamin-b12-deficiency.blurb: Gradual fatigue with numb, with pallor.
hem-vitamin-b12-deficiency.summary: Vitamin B12 deficiency presents with gradual fatigue with numb, tingling feet and unsteady gait, typically with pallor, reduced vibratory sense, and impaired position sense at the toes. Serum B12 with methylmalonic acid confirmation confirms it, and parenteral B12 repletion is the initial management.

sections.heading: Overview
paras: Vitamin B12 deficiency is defined by gradual fatigue with numb, tingling feet and unsteady gait, arising from impaired DNA synthesis with dorsal column demyelination. The account that follows moves from the underlying process to the bedside picture, then to confirmation and initial treatment — the order in which the problem is usually met.

Reported frequency varies with the population studied and with the threshold chosen to define a case, so figures quoted in different sources are rarely directly comparable. The teaching point most often attached to this topic is that treating with folate alone corrects the blood and abandons the spinal cord.

sections.heading: Mechanism
paras: What drives the picture is impaired DNA synthesis with dorsal column demyelination. Its consequences account for both the symptoms the patient reports and the signs found on examination.

Reserve within the affected system means measurable derangement often precedes anything the patient notices. Understanding this is what makes parenteral B12 repletion the rational first response rather than an arbitrary one.

sections.heading: Clinical presentation
paras: Gradual fatigue with numb, tingling feet and unsteady gait is the complaint that brings the patient in, and its evolution over days to weeks is the detail worth pinning down.

Comorbid disease alters the picture, sometimes to the point that the usual pattern is unrecognisable. A history of gradual fatigue with numb, tingling feet and unsteady gait in the right context is enough to bring the diagnosis to the front of the differential.

sections.heading: Examination

hem-polycythemia-vera.title: Polycythemia vera
hem-polycythemia-vera.blurb: Generalized itching after hot showers with persistent facial redness; first step, serial phlebotomy with low-dose aspirin.
hem-polycythemia-vera.summary: Polycythemia vera presents with generalized itching after hot showers with persistent facial redness, typically with facial plethora with splenomegaly and an elevated hematocrit. Erythropoietin level with driver mutation testing confirms it, and serial phlebotomy with low-dose aspirin is the initial management.

sections.heading: Overview
paras: The presentation that names polycythemia vera is generalized itching after hot showers with persistent facial redness; the process behind it is a clonal kinase mutation driving erythropoietin-independent red cell production. Sections below follow one conventional sequence — mechanism, presentation, confirmation, management — and each can be read on its own.

Reported frequency varies with the population studied and with the threshold chosen to define a case, so figures quoted in different sources are rarely directly comparable. The teaching point most often attached to this topic is that a suppressed erythropoietin level separates true polycythemia from its reactive mimics.

sections.heading: Mechanism
paras: At the centre of the problem is a clonal kinase mutation driving erythropoietin-independent red cell production. Tracing the picture back to that single process explains why the individual findings travel together rather than appearing in isolation.

Compensatory responses mask the process early and fail late, which is why the interval between the first abnormality and the first symptom can be long. Understanding this is what makes serial phlebotomy with low-dose aspirin the rational first response rather than an arbitrary one.

sections.heading: Clinical presentation
paras: The history classically centres on generalized itching after hot showers with persistent facial redness; what refines it is the time course rather than the severity at any one moment.

Partial or atypical presentations are common enough that the absence of one expected feature should not close the question. A history of generalized itching after hot showers with persistent facial redness in the right context is enough to bring the diagnosis to the front of the differential.

sections.heading: Examination
paras: The sign to look for is facial plethora with splenomegaly and an elevated hematocrit; it is more specific than the rest of the examination and is worth eliciting carefully.
Interobserver agreement for the classic signs is only moderate, which is a reason to weigh them alongside the history rather than above it.
